attestations.value: The source mentions that Astypalaia provided safe anchorages for corsairs.

citations.exact_excerpt:
At the same time, Astypalaia was an excellent hideout for corsairs, not only because they could ﬁnd provisions there (such as bread, wine, etc.) and stock up with drinking water, but also because the island provided
plenty of safe anchorages.

attestations.value: The passage states that a Catholic church honoring Saint George was built by the Tuscan corsair Francesco Barbieri in Ayionissi in 1695.

citations.exact_excerpt:
The local tradition of the Frankish origins of the church is
ultimately verified by the records of the French consulate of Melos, which refer to a 1695 decision of capitan
generale Antonio Zeno, acknowledging that the Tuscan corsair Francesco Barbieri had built a Catholic church
honoring Saint George in Ayionissi (CADN, Milo et l’Argentière 3, 216).

honoring Saint George in Ayionissi (CADN, Milo et l’Argentière 3, 216).

attestations.value: The study references letters from embassies and consuls in Izmir during the second half of the 17th century, including Agostino Spinola and others, as primary sources.

citations.exact_excerpt:

Giustiniani and Ottavio Doria, Luigi Cartabono, Simon Massa and Giovanni Luigi Gentile.

attestations.value: The source reports that Dieudé left Crete in 1686 and settled in Milos, collaborating with Ottoman adversaries.

citations.exact_excerpt:
Il est donc tout à fait compréhensible que
l’ambassadeur Girardin, informé de la concurrence illicite provoquée par Dieudé
dans le négoce français, fît quelques démarches en 1686 pour qu’il fût expulsé
de l’île et renvoyé à Marseille.28 Et c’est ainsi que finalement, la même année,
Dieudé quitta la Crète;29 mais il n’alla pas très loin: il s’installa à Milos et, cette
fois-ci, il collabora avec les adversaires des Ottomans.

attestations.value: The Barbary Coast became a base of operations for corsairs spreading to Malta and Livorno.

citations.exact_excerpt:
Throughout the latter seventeenth century, Constan- 
tinople's control over its North African vassals declined and the Barbary 
Coast became a base of operations for corsairs whose activities spread to 
Malta and Livorno in Italy.
